subject: Post-call: PayMate discovery — token economics & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@paymate.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: PayMate discovery — token economics & pilot next steps

Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap so we have alignment and a clear set of next steps.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-transaction cost sensitivity: finance expects < $0.005 average token-equivalent cost for the customer-facing flows.
- Burst traffic during settlement windows causes latency spikes and customer complaints.
- Compliance: need audit logs and SOC2 evidence for pilot.

Goals you outlined:
- Run a 6-week pilot of 50k sessions/day focused on transaction enrichment and fraud signal generation.
- Validate 30–40% effective token-burn reduction with batching + prefix caching while maintaining model accuracy.
- Get procurement approval with a capped pilot spend and an option to convert to Dedicated if latency SLOs are met.

Economic levers we discussed (high level):
- Model selection: medium-sized open model vs smaller quantized variant — tradeoff between raw quality and token cost.
- Batching: session micro-batching during settlement windows to reduce per-token latency overheads.
- Prefix/KV caching: persist common context across requests to cut repeated prompt tokens by ~20–35%.
- Fallback routing: route non-critical requests to cheaper model variants when Dedicated capacity is constrained.

Attached: PayMate-pilot-estimate.xlsx (pilot cost scenarios) and a short Redwood TCO one-pager.

Proposed immediate next steps (can we confirm by EOD Friday?):
1) You to confirm pilot target (sessions/day) and any hard budget cap for the 6-week run.
2) Security questionnaire: I’ll loop in our security team; please share the primary contact at security@paymate.com.
3) Redwood to deliver a 2-page pilot SOW + estimated cost ranges (we’ll provide three scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive).
4) Tech sync next week (30m) to map data flows and discuss KMS and audit log specifics — propose Tue 2026-07-07 10:00 AM PT if that works.

If anything above is off, tell me and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll move forward on the SOW and a scoped cost scenario workbook.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193
Redwood Inference

Attachments: PayMate-pilot-estimate.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB), redwood-tco-one-pager.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@paymate.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@paymate.com>, security@paymate.com
Date: 2026-07-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayMate discovery — token economics & pilot next steps

Thanks Grace — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Pilot targets: we’re comfortable starting at 40k sessions/day with a stretch to 60k/day in week 4 if performance holds. Budget cap: $45k total for the 6-week pilot (including any infra costs).

2) Cost sensitivity: $0.005 avg token-equivalent is a long-term target; for the pilot our procurement will accept up to $0.01/token if we can show clear path to sub-$0.005 with batching/caching within 4 weeks.

3) Compliance contact: adding our security lead so she sees the thread — Michael Chen (mchen@paymate.com). He’ll send the standard data-flow and DFARS/SOC2 checklist this afternoon.

4) Tech sync: Tue 2026-07-07 10:00 AM PT works. Please send calendar invite.

Two asks for your SOW/cost workbook: include a short sensitivity table showing cost vs. batch size (1,4,8) and vs. cache hit-rate (0%,15%,30%). That will help our finance and infra teams triage.

—Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-04T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayMate discovery — token economics & pilot next steps

Alex / team — thanks for the quick clarity. A couple of engineering-focused notes that we'll include in the SOW and the cost workbook: 

• Batching sensitivity: our measurements on comparable workloads show the following rough per-token cost multipliers (relative to batch=1): batch=4 -> ~0.72x, batch=8 -> ~0.60x, with diminishing returns after 8 for latency-sensitive requests.

• Prefix/KV caching: typical hit rates for transaction enrichment contexts with short canonical prompts are in the 20–30% range after a warm-up period; that leads to 18–28% token reduction in practice and material CPU/GPU time saving. We'll include a conservative/expected/aggressive hit-rate assumption table.

• Model variants & fallback: recommend modeling three variants in the workbook — standard (stable open model), quantized-mid (lower cost, small accuracy delta), and fallback-lite (low-cost, for non-critical background tasks). We'll show expected accuracy/latency/cost tradeoffs.

• Observability: pilot will include token-level cost breakdowns per route and a dashboard with monthlyized extrapolation to your projected 1M sessions/day baseline.

Action items from our side:
1) I’ll produce the cost-workbook with sensitivity tables (batch size x cache hit-rate x model variant) by end of day Mon 2026-07-06.
2) Grace will send the SOW + calendar invite for Tue 2026-07-07 10:00 AM PT.
3) Michael — if you attach the security checklist we’ll start mapping required artifacts against Redwood’s SOC2 docs (attachments included).

Ben Carter
